policy_title: Cabinet Minister for Children and Young People
stated: Appoint a Cabinet Minister for Children and Young People. Protect and support the rights and wellbeing of every child by: Incorporating the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child into UK law. Setting up an independent advocacy body for children’s safety online. Addressing the underfunding and neglect of children’s mental health services, youth services and youth justice services. Tackling child poverty. Giving 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote.

source.quote: Appoint a Cabinet Minister for Children and Young People. Protect and support the rights and wellbeing of every child by: Incorporating the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child into UK law. Setting up an independent advocacy body for children’s safety online. Addressing the underfunding and neglect of children’s mental health services, youth services and youth justice services. Tackling child poverty, as set out in chapter 10. Giving 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote, as set out in chapter 20.

bearing_set.reason: Explicitly commits to addressing underfunding of children's mental health services, directly affecting healthcare access and waiting times for a high-need group.
Youth justice services reform bears on the justice system for young people; independent children's online safety advocacy body bears on children's safety from online harm.
Youth services investment and tackling child poverty both have well-established links to educational attainment gaps and life-chances for disadvantaged children.

Incorporating the UNCRC into UK law is a legal-rights framework change; extending the vote to 16- and 17-year-olds is a direct democratic/voting rights measure — both squarely within O9's strict scope.
Explicitly pledges to tackle child poverty, which directly affects real disposable income and ability to afford essentials for lower-income families with children.
Tackling child poverty directly narrows the income and resource gap between low-income families and the rest — a core O14 indicator.

membership_note: Policy bundles five substantively distinct sub-commitments targeting different outcomes: mental health (O3), youth justice (O5), children's rights and voting age (O9), child poverty as distributional gap (O14), and child poverty as essentials affordability (O2). The Cabinet Minister appointment and online safety advocacy body are machinery-of-government or process measures whose downstream effects are too unspecified to earn a non-negligible verdict on any additional fundamental.
